policy: Every `pub fn` this gate reports as unwired (zero references anywhere, `tests/` included) must be listed here with a `kind` and a real `why`. An entry is a decision to leave a public function unwired — the one thing a reader cannot re-derive from the code — so the reason lives *here*, next to the entry, and not only in prose. Enforced by scripts/rust-unwired-scan.mjs (REQ-A445): R1 an entry with no real `why` fails, R2 an entry whose symbol is referenced now fails (the ratchet must shrink, not rot), R3 a duplicate fails. `--update-baseline` keeps existing reasons and marks a new entry `UNREVIEWED` with a placeholder R1 refuses, so a writer can never silently excuse a new finding. Kinds: `library-surface` (public API a consumer composes), `planned-feature` (the unwired half of a feature whose write side exists), `inspection-api` (accessor a host may call), `host-missing` (helper whose host/test does not exist yet). The prose rationale for each kind is in docs/rust-unwired-audit.md.

entries.why: Maintenance entry point on a public service so a host can flush the manager's cache; the daemon surfaces the underlying state through its own RPC/status path, so no in-workspace caller needs it yet.

Accessor exposing the client's Android bridge handle so a host can inspect the installed backend; the installed-app registry lives in the System UI (crates/amos-tauri/src/appstore.rs), and amos-ai does not link amos-appstore at all, so the bridge is reachable only through this crate's own API — hence no in-workspace caller.
Fluent constructor on a public model type; in-workspace callers build the struct directly (or via `Default`), so it is unused today — deleting it would shrink the library API for no defect fixed.

Fluent constructor so a caller can pin a recognizer's language in one expression; in-workspace callers pass the language per call instead, so the builder has no caller today but is part of the public API.
Fluent constructor on a public spec type: it exists so a consumer can compose a value in one expression, while the in-workspace callers build the struct directly — unused today, and not a defect.
Read-only accessor naming the sampler a monitor is using, exposed so a host can inspect it; the daemon reports the same fact through its status path, so there is no in-workspace caller yet.

Convenience constructor for a DNS `EgressEvent`, on public API. The prior reason here ('no production caller constructs that event yet, so the constructor has no host') was false: the production wire mapping `event_from_req` (crates/amos-ai/src/netguard_service.rs) DOES build DNS-kind `EgressEvent`s — but as a full struct literal, because it must carry the request's own `app`/`bytes` (this constructor hardcodes `app: ""`/`bytes: 0`, so wiring it would *drop* those fields). The tests likewise build literals. So the true state is a public convenience constructor with no in-workspace caller, not a feature whose host is missing.
Documented as 'recompute after a caller mutates `text`' — and no caller in the workspace mutates `text`, so there is nothing to refresh; the helper waits for the mutating path to exist.
Read-only accessor returning the frequency plan actually applied, exposed so a host can inspect it; the state is already surfaced through the daemon's status path, so no in-workspace caller needs it.
Fluent constructor on a public policy type so a consumer can set the high-temperature threshold in one expression; in-workspace callers build the struct directly, so it is unused today.
Fluent constructor on the Android profiling type so a consumer can supply the voltage in one expression; the in-workspace caller fills the field directly, so the builder has no caller today.

Read-only accessor counting what one conversation has in the SMS trash. The trash itself is System-UI-owned (crates/amos-tauri/src/sms.rs holds SmsTrashState and serves sms_trash_list/restore/purge); amos-ai has no SMS surface, and the UI reads the whole entries() list rather than a per-thread count, so nothing in the workspace calls it yet.
Read-only accessor telling whether the Android glue is installed, for a host that wants to inspect it; the host-side path reports the same state through its own command, so there is no caller yet.
Read-only accessor giving the installed name of a package, exposed for host inspection; the app store reads the same information through its own store path, so no in-workspace caller needs it.

Half-wired device feature (REQ-A411): Kotlin writes a discovered NFC tag into this host-side cell, but nothing reads it — a non-consuming peek has no caller until an `nfc_*` command exists (screen + i18n + a device run), which is the missing piece.

Half-wired device feature (REQ-A411): Kotlin callbacks deposit a BLE GATT notification value here, but no host command consumes it; the BLE half is otherwise wired (`arm_services` / `disarm_services` / `deliver_services`, plus the `arm_read` / `deliver_read` pair that the REQ-A413 fix put in place of its single-slot predecessor), so this is the remaining read side, not dead code. The single-slot BLE state accessor this line once named was deleted by REQ-A1157; ble.rs now arms and delivers through the pairs above — the name had to go, or this ledger would cite code that no longer exists (the REQ-A828 / F-DEV-103 shape).

Half-wired device feature (REQ-A411): the consuming reader of the discovered NFC tag; its author already marked it `#[allow(dead_code)]`, i.e. the intent was recorded but never turned into a wiring — the missing piece is an `nfc_*` command, not the accessor.

Fluent constructor on the timekeeper so a consumer can name it in one expression; in-workspace callers build the struct directly (or via `Default`), so it is unused today and deleting it would only shrink the API.
SEC1 compressed-to-uncompressed key conversion; it needs a caller that actually consumes uncompressed keys, and no such path exists in the workspace yet, so the helper has no host.

The second rung of the `serve*` ladder (log sink + JSON sink). `crates/amos-ai/src/main.rs:117` reaches `serve_with_sinks_full` directly, because the production boot must also hand over the notifier sink and this rung has no notifier parameter — so it is the public API for an embedder that wants exactly those two sinks. The behaviour it documents is live (the binary passes `json_sink.handle()` one rung down); only this entry point is unused. Verified with an independent comment-aware scan: the declaration is the only *code* occurrence of the name in the workspace.

The canonical 4-layer resolver (system file -> user file -> env -> remote), whose doc says it is 'provided because this is the shape every daemon and the System UI wants'. No daemon builds it: every construction site in the workspace composes its own `ResolverBuilder` chain, usually a deliberate subset (env-only in `reload.rs`'s own tests; the examples build file+env). The `Resolver` type itself is live (`reload.rs`, `feature_flag.rs`), so only the word 'every' in that doc is false. Recomposing 4 layers by hand at each site is the current shape; this constructor is convenience surface with no caller.

One `Telemetry` snapshot plus the instantaneous board power sampled from a live `PowerSource` — the reading the `PowerDraw` policy branch needs. Unreferenced: not production, not a test, and not the governor example (`live_governor.rs` builds `Telemetry::new(...)` with `None` power). The fold it delegates to (`Telemetry::with_power_from`) *is* exercised — line 112 of this crate's linux test `closed_loop_linux.rs`, the example `live_governor.rs`, and three cases in `types.rs` — so what is absent is the on-device `AndroidBatteryPowerSource` producer, not the arithmetic. `host-missing`.

Its doc says 'called from MainActivity.onStart via JNI'; it is not. The live install path is `Java_com_amos_ai_glue_BluetoothGattGlue_nativeInstall` (`crates/amos-tauri/src/jni_glue.rs:346`, which calls `jni_glue::init()` at :395) plus `crates/amos-tauri/src/lib.rs:873` — so the three `OnceLock` states it would arm are armed. This third path (`android_jni::install` + `glue_state::init()`) calls two things that are both reached elsewhere and is kept as the Rust-side install entry; the doc comment was corrected to say so (REQ-A832).

Snapshot of the event bus's counters (subscribers / dropped / evicted) for diagnostics and tests. No test and no command asks for it: the bus's behaviour is asserted through the clipboard commands themselves, and `bus_stats` is the accessor an operator-side diagnostic would call. `inspection-api` — read-only, no side effects, honest about being unasked today.

Builds the bridge over a real `AndroidFlashlightProvider`. The on-device path does not use it: `Java_com_amos_ai_glue_FlashlightGlue_attach` (same file, :274) constructs the provider itself and stores it in `DEVICE`/`TORCH_PRESENT` — a different shape (the trampoline installs a provider; this returns a bridge wrapper over one). So it is a second, unused constructor of the same provider; the wiring it looks like it performs is already done, and the desktop Mock path is unaffected.

On-device attach of a real `AndroidSensorProvider` (GNSS via `LocationManager`). The live path is `Java_com_amos_ai_glue_SensorGlue_attachContext` (same file, :312) -> `android_ctx::bind(vm, &env, ctx)`, which is what makes the snapshot's `gnss` real and which warns loudly on failure (REQ-A187); this `&self` method is a second attach that nothing calls. `library-surface`: the capability is wired, this entry point is not the one that wires it.

Merges a live `outer_position` into a state's `x/y`; its doc says 'used when applying a saved state'. No apply path calls it. Its sibling `with_size` is invisible to this gate for the other half of F-DEV-066 — the name is shared by `devocare::AppPackage::with_size` (`crates/amos-tauri/src/devcare.rs:1071`), and a bare-name count cannot tell two same-named methods apart, so one covers for the other. The restore path reads the OS geometry in `snapshot()` and the saved rectangle through the store; the merge is convenience surface with no caller.

Simulates the remote party hanging up — the partner of the desktop demo's auto-connect (`ProviderEvent::RemoteEnded` -> the service's state machine at `service.rs:236`). Nothing calls it: the telephony e2e harness mounts `mock_server` and never drives this hook, and `provider.rs:285` cites it only in prose. `inspection-api`: a handle for moving the mock provider's state directly, unused today.

Its doc says 'used by the amos-ai daemon for the desktop demo'; the daemon mounts the **limited** sibling instead — `crates/amos-ai/src/server.rs:2360` adds `amos_telephony::service::demo_server_limited(30)` (ordinary-dial rate limiting, emergency exempt). So this unlimited variant is the same server minus the limiter, with no caller of its own; the tests use `mock_server`.

The **only** legitimate writer of a push-permission change (REQ-A865): a platform glue that the OS has just answered is meant to call it, and nothing in this tree does yet because `permission_backend` is `None` on every target — this build ships no push-permission backend at all. `push_request_permission` used to call it, which is exactly how the panel came to announce a grant nobody made; that caller was removed, leaving the method with zero callers and no other doorway. It is kept rather than deleted because it is the single place a future glue must land — its own doc comment is what stops the fabrication returning as the path of least resistance — and the read side that glue would pair with is `push_get_permission`. Deleting it would take the guard rail out with the unused method.
